date.label: Undated Ruth narrative
date.note: Biblical narrative chronology is not independently established as an absolute BCE date.

claims.claim: A *petuchah* `{P}` break stands between Ruth 4:17 and 4:18, closing the narrative before the genealogy begins; a further `{P}` closes the book at 4:22.
claims.evidence: Mechon Mamre Ruth 4 page, read live 2026-11-23: `{P}` after v. 17 and at the end of v. 22.

claims.claim: The list contains ten names in order: Perez, Hezron, Ram, Amminadab, Nahshon, Salmah/Salmon, Boaz, Obed, Jesse, David.
claims.evidence: Hebrew text read live (Mechon Mamre); each name checked verse by verse (§3.1).

claims.claim: The list is a bare "begot" list: no scene, dialogue, place, time, or mention of Ruth or Naomi, unlike Ruth 4:1–17.
claims.evidence: Text itself, read live; genre contrast stated in the read record and confirmed against the Mechon Mamre page.

claims.claim: Verses 21–22 repeat the Boaz–Obed–Jesse–David chain already given in Ruth 4:17, anchoring the narrative's endpoint into a longer lineage.
claims.evidence: Ruth 4:17 and 4:21–22 read live; identical chain in both places.

claims.claim: Perez, the head of the list, is the son of Judah by Tamar (Gen 38:29), already named in the elders' blessing at Ruth 4:12.
claims.evidence: K&D (Perez "a son of Judah by Tamar (Gen 38:29)"); Cambridge Bible (list "attached to Perez, because he is named in Ruth 4:12"); Gen 38 levirate background reused from `clm-deu-06-067` (established). Gen 38 text not re-read live this session.

claims.claim: The list is selective (telescoped): it omits intermediate generations and cannot be read as a complete generation-by-generation record.
claims.evidence: K&D (too few generations for 430 years in Egypt; two generations for 250+ years after the exodus); JFB (380 years between Salmon and David; "whole generations are omitted"); Ellicott ("designedly left out"); Ron (ellipsis at Salma). Year-counts differ between commentaries and were not independently recomputed.

claims.claim: The list divides into two halves of five names — Perez to Nahshon, and Salmon to David — with Nahshon as the hinge at the exodus generation.
claims.evidence: K&D (five links to the Egyptian sojourn, five from Salmon to David); Ron (Nahshon–Salma transition at "the exact middle"). The division is interpretive; Nahshon's dates are not given in the text.

claims.claim: Salmah (Ruth 4:20) and Salmon (Ruth 4:21) are two forms of the same name, the same person in the same slot; 1 Chr 2:11 gives Salma.
claims.evidence: Hebrew text read live (שַׂלְמָה v. 20, שַׂלְמוֹן v. 21); 1 Chr 2:11 read live (KJV, "Salma"); K&D on the double form (elision of the *n*).

claims.claim: The list's purpose is to trace David's descent from Perez and thereby to present the book as the family history of David's ancestors.
claims.evidence: K&D ("an evident proof that the book was intended to give a family picture … of … king David"); JFB ("to trace the genealogy of David"); Constable (the appendix "ties the events … to the past as well as to the future"). Purpose is interpretive, inferred from the ending.

claims.claim: The opening formula "these are the generations" (*toledot*) is the same formula that heads the Genesis genealogies (Gen 5:1; 11:10; also Gen 2:4; 6:9; 10:1).
claims.evidence: BDB H8435 (Ruth 4:18 listed with Gen 2:4, 5:1, 6:9, 10:1, 11:10, 11:27); Cambridge Bible ("standing formulae of P").

claims.claim: The same Perez-to-David line is reproduced in Matthew 1:3–6 (Grecised names; Tamar, Rahab, and Ruth named) and in Luke 3:31–33 (reversed order).
claims.evidence: Matt 1:3–6 read live (KJV); 1 Chr 2:5–15 read live for the same thread. Luke 3 not read live this session; rests on the Pulpit Commentary ("incorporated entire in the two tables").

claims.claim: 1 Chronicles 2:15 makes David Jesse's seventh son; 1 Samuel 16:10–11 counts him as the eighth son presented. The two counts differ and are not reconciled here.
claims.evidence: 1 Chr 2:13–15 read live (KJV, "David the seventh"); Ron n. 7 notes the 1 Sam 16 conflict and cites Radak's resolutions, which were not read. 1 Sam 16 text not read live this session.

claims.claim: Ten names mark a complete, epoch-opening list: David in tenth position begins the Davidic monarchy as Noah (tenth from Adam) began the post-Flood world and Abraham (twentieth) began Israel.
claims.evidence: Ron (ten-generation epochs; David tenth; Boaz seventh echoing Enoch seventh in Gen 5); K&D ("the number ten as the seal of completeness"). Intentionality is asserted, not demonstrated, by these sources; Sasson pp. 183–184 (seventh/tenth prominence) known only via Ron.

claims.claim: Whether any of the ten named men is independently attested outside the biblical text is not established by the research for this dossier.
claims.evidence: No extra-biblical attestation of any of the ten names was identified; no archaeological evidence bears on the list (§6). Absence of a find is not proof of non-existence.

claims.claim: The list gives no date and cannot be used as a clock: ten generations do not yield a datable chronology for the Perez-to-David span.
claims.evidence: Text gives no date; K&D/JFB/Ron arithmetic shows the span exceeds ten lifetimes under any traditional year-count, but the commentaries disagree on the year-counts themselves (§7.1). Date of the category is unknown.

connections.note: The elders' blessing names Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah; the genealogy opens with that same Perez.
The neighbours name Obed and add that he is the father of Jesse, the father of David; the list repeats that chain.
The birth of Perez and his twin Zerah to Tamar, the head of the list's own origin.
Hezron is named among the sons of Judah who went down into Egypt with Jacob.
The clan of Perez is named after him, showing why the list starts at the clan founder.
Amminadab's daughter Elisheba marries Aaron, tying the list's fourth name to the priestly house.
Nahshon is named as prince of the tribe of Judah at the census in the wilderness.
The same Perez-to-David line, fuller: brothers and sisters are kept, and David is Jesse's seventh son.
The same line retold with Grecised names, naming Tamar, Rahab, and Ruth, and continuing past David to Solomon.
The same line in reverse order, from David back through Jesse, Obed, Boaz, Salmon, and Nahshon to Perez.
The promise of an enduring house to David's offspring gives the list's endpoint its forward meaning.
Jacob's blessing places the ruler's staff with Judah, the tribe from which the list's line descends.
Ten generations from Adam to Noah, the formal model for a ten-name list marking one era's close.
Ten generations from Shem to Abraham, the second ten-name list, marking the turn toward Israel.
The book's only time anchor, placing the story in the days when the judges judged.
David is anointed as Jesse's youngest son; the count of Jesse's sons differs from the Chronicles list and is left unresolved here.
A rabbinic tradition identifies Boaz with Ibzan of Bethlehem, the judge named here; the identification is reported, not asserted.
